channel.description: Plain-English daily summaries of Microsoft Purview documentation and Message Center changes.

item.title: Purview review and investigation summaries are unavailable across all tenants — 26 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 26 November 2026

Purview review and investigation summaries are unavailable across all tenants

The most consequential update is temporary loss of summarization: eDiscovery and Security Investigations say Summarize is unavailable for all tenants, while Communication Compliance reviewers cannot generate contextual summaries for flagged communications. Updated DLP guidance makes encrypted-message branding prerequisites explicit, and Browser DLP guidance changes its documented Edge for Business baseline from version 144 to 158.

eDiscovery · General

eDiscovery Summarize is unavailable for every tenant

Updated eDiscovery guidance says Summarize is unavailable for all tenants: the option is hidden, administrators cannot generate item summaries, and they cannot ask Security Copilot questions about review set items. The documented impact is a temporary disruption to these review set functions.

Security Investigations · Alerts, reports and investigation

Security Investigations item summaries are unavailable

The Security Investigations guidance now says Summarize is unavailable for all tenants. The option no longer appears when reviewing an item, and summaries cannot be generated; investigators therefore cannot use item summarization during this period.

Communication Compliance · Alerts, reports and investigation

Communication Compliance loses contextual summaries for flagged communications

Updated guidance says reviewers cannot generate contextual summaries for communications flagged for potential policy violations. Reviewers must investigate those communications without Copilot-generated contextual summaries until the capability becomes available again.

Data Loss Prevention · Policies and rules

DLP branding requires an existing Message Encryption template

The DLP Policy Reference now states that the action requires an existing Microsoft Purview Message Encryption branding template and does not encrypt messages itself. It should be used in Exchange-only policies for internal senders, and the guidance documents the external-recipient portal option.

Data Loss Prevention · General

Browser DLP’s documented Edge baseline moves to version 158

The documented baseline for Browser DLP changes from Edge for Business version 144 to version 158, covering the two latest stable versions. Administrators should check managed Edge for Business versions to ensure Browser DLP features remain supported.

View all updates for 26 November 2026 →

item.title: Legacy Teams retention policies become Teams-only as Copilot coverage moves separately — 25 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 25 November 2026

Legacy Teams retention policies become Teams-only as Copilot coverage moves separately

Starting in mid-January 2027, legacy Microsoft Teams retention policies will apply only to Teams data and exclude Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. Organizations that need Copilot retention must create separate policies. The period also brings a staged Communication Compliance alert enhancement and documentation updates covering DSI billing, Fabric Graph audit activities, and encryption access guidance.

Purview · AI and Copilot

Legacy Teams retention policies become Teams-only for Copilot coverage

Starting mid-January 2027, legacy Microsoft Teams retention policies will exclude Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. Separate retention policies are required to retain Copilot data, while existing Teams retention behavior remains unchanged.

Purview · Alerts, reports and investigation

Communication Compliance policy alerts get frequency and recipient controls

The announced enhancement will let administrators adjust policy-alert frequency and recipients, with pseudonymized usernames, role-based access, and audit logs included. The stated schedule places public preview in October 2026 and general availability by mid-August 2027.

Security Investigations · Licensing and billing

DSI billing page drops compute-unit deletion steps

The page now states that deleting all investigations stops storage billing, but the steps for deleting the DSI compute unit capacity resource to stop AI capacity and compute billing were removed.

Audit · General

Audit activity reference adds Fabric Graph query and load entries

The Audit Log Activities page now documents Run Graph Query and Run Load Graph Data, including their activity names and generation conditions. Load and refresh entries include success or failure status.

Information Protection · General

Encryption guidance revises supported cloud-pairing and contact language

The page now lists Commercial-to-Government/China, Government-to-Commercial, and China-to-Commercial access. It removes the statement that access could be enabled without contacting Microsoft.

View all updates for 25 November 2026 →

item.title: Azure Firewall prerequisites expand as Purview documents rolling adaptive-scope date filters — 24 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 24 November 2026

Azure Firewall prerequisites expand as Purview documents rolling adaptive-scope date filters

The strongest updates are operational guidance for Data Loss Prevention, DSPM, and Purview adaptive scopes. Network Data Security material now spells out Azure Firewall integration prerequisites and coverage, while a new adaptive-scope article documents rolling date filters for users, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites. Information Protection adds per-SKU licensing and label-interaction detail for auto-labeling. Data Lifecycle’s priority-cleanup procedure now sets explicit approval and recovery conditions for permanent deletion involving legal holds.

Data Loss Prevention · Fundamentals

DLP Network Data Security guidance specifies Azure Firewall prerequisites

The updated Network Data Security article documents Azure Firewall integration, including required Purview licensing, Azure Firewall Premium with the AI Security add-on, and a supported-region prerequisite. It says Azure Firewall and Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access support all activities and actions, and neither requires pay-as-you-go setup.

DSPM · Planning and deployment

DSPM collection-policy guidance adds Azure Firewall as an integration option

The collection-policy deployment guidance now lists Azure Firewall as an integration, says Microsoft Purview pay-as-you-go billing is not required for it, and links to configuration instructions.

Purview · General

Adaptive-scope guidance documents rolling date filters across users, groups, and sites

A new article explains supported properties and query syntax for rolling date filters on users, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites. Custom SharePoint dates require site metadata and managed-property mapping, and retention settings remain separate.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Information Protection guidance ties auto-labeling to licensing and label interactions

The auto-labeling page now points to the current per-SKU licensing matrix, separates requirements by shared-location role, and explains interactions with library defaults and existing labels. It also adds policy failure-code guidance, with specific licensing implications for SharePoint owners and members.

Data Lifecycle · General

Priority Cleanup guidance now requires approval before deleting legally held items

The procedure explicitly requires administrator approval for items under legal hold. Deleted SharePoint and OneDrive content bypasses recycle bins; an inaccessible protected copy may remain for up to 90 days, while recovery is exceptional, support-mediated, and not guaranteed.

View all updates for 24 November 2026 →

item.title: Unified Catalog guidance now records the no-new-account rule and November 12, 2027 timeline — 21 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 21 November 2026

Unified Catalog guidance now records the no-new-account rule and November 12, 2027 timeline

This was largely a documentation-maintenance day. Updated guidance across Data Governance and related Purview pages consistently says Unified Catalog and classic data governance capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric: new data governance accounts cannot be created, while existing capabilities remain in maintenance mode through November 12, 2027. The guidance distinguishes unaffected data security and compliance capabilities. The main separate change is a DLP reference update for short pasted text.

Data Governance · Planning and deployment

Retirement guidance standardizes the scope, account restriction, and Fabric destination

The updated Unified Catalog plan states that Unified Catalog and classic data governance capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric. New governance accounts cannot be created, existing capabilities remain in maintenance mode through November 12, 2027, and security and compliance capabilities are unaffected.

Data Loss Prevention · Policies and rules

DLP Paste to Browser coverage now has explicit short-text thresholds

The DLP Policy Reference says Paste to Browser does not evaluate text smaller than 15 characters or 30 bytes. Administrators should use those thresholds when assessing DLP coverage for short pasted text.

View all updates for 21 November 2026 →

item.title: eDiscovery guidance separates mailbox-copy and permanent Teams-message purges — 19 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 November 2026

eDiscovery guidance separates mailbox-copy and permanent Teams-message purges

An updated eDiscovery page clarifies two different purge paths: cmdlet purges affect only mailbox compliance copies, while Microsoft Graph purges targeting `teamsMessages` permanently delete Teams messages regardless of `purgeType`. Purging both representations requires separate requests.

eDiscovery · General

Purge guidance distinguishes compliance-copy and Teams-message deletion

The updated guidance states that cmdlet purges apply only to mailbox compliance copies. Graph requests targeting `teamsMessages` permanently delete Teams messages regardless of `purgeType`, and separate requests are required to purge both copies.

item.title: eDiscovery Graph guidance documents permanent Teams purges and GCC export-auth limits — 18 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 November 2026

eDiscovery Graph guidance documents permanent Teams purges and GCC export-auth limits

The day’s most consequential changes are operational eDiscovery constraints: Teams-message purges are documented as permanent regardless of `purgeType`, must be requested separately from mailbox purges, and run first; a separate export guide adds a GCC restriction on app-based authentication. A forward-looking Message Center announcement schedules DLP and auto-labeling for connected non-Microsoft apps starting mid-March 2027, while other updates clarify Agent Builder Information Barriers behavior and SAP S/4HANA scan sizing.

eDiscovery · General

Teams-message purges are documented as permanent, with a required sequence

The eDiscovery guidance states that `teamsMessages` purges permanently delete Teams messages regardless of `purgeType`. Mailbox and Teams purges require separate requests, with Teams first; the API returns `202 Accepted` and a status URL.

eDiscovery · Developer and PowerShell

GCC cannot use app-based authentication for Graph eDiscovery export downloads

The export guide adds the GCC limitation and clarifies the application IDs, scopes, and authentication parameters required by its scripts. Administrators should replace placeholder values with the correct MicrosoftPurviewEDiscovery application ID; GCC administrators cannot use app-based authentication for export downloads.

Purview · Labels and classification

Purview schedules DLP and auto-labeling for connected non-Microsoft apps

A Message Center notice says Purview will support DLP and auto-labeling for apps such as Google Workspace, Box, and Salesforce through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps connectors. Administrators can manage the policies directly in Purview starting mid-March 2027.

Communication Compliance · General

Agent Builder guidance says Information Barriers hide restricted users

The Information Barriers guidance adds that Agent Builder honors Information Barriers policies in its people picker, hiding users whom a person is restricted from communicating or collaborating with.

Data Governance · General

SAP S/4HANA scan guidance sets a 128 GB RAM recommendation

The source-registration guidance now identifies SAP S/4HANA, rather than SAP ECC, as the memory-intensive scan requiring a recommended Self-hosted Integration Runtime machine with at least 128 GB of RAM.

View all updates for 18 November 2026 →

item.title: Adaptive protection preview targets 120-day labels for high-risk-user deletions — 17 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 17 November 2026

Adaptive protection preview targets 120-day labels for high-risk-user deletions

Data Lifecycle Management’s Adaptive protection integration is the standout capability change: the public preview automatically applies retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users for 120 days, with general availability listed for early 2027. Other meaningful updates cover 2027 PST Import planning, a Teams Information Barriers procedure, Clipchamp label inheritance, and more precise auto-label reporting guidance.

Purview · General

Adaptive protection integrates with Data Lifecycle Management

The public-preview integration automatically applies retention labels to content deleted by elevated-risk users for 120 days. Microsoft lists general availability for early 2027 and describes the setup as requiring minimal administrator configuration.

Purview · General

Azure PST Import is scheduled to begin in April 2027

Admins will import PST files from Azure Blob Storage into Exchange Online mailboxes through PowerShell, with readiness analysis and import batching. The rollout requires specified Azure permissions and mailbox prerequisites, and imported data remains subject to existing retention and audit policies.

Communication Compliance · General

Information Barriers guidance documents Explicit-mode Teams conversion

The updated guidance explains how to change a Teams-connected Microsoft 365 group from Implicit to Explicit mode with PowerShell. It documents segment-based access and membership, up to 24 hours for segment stamping, and the restriction that site owners and SharePoint admins cannot manage segments on Explicit-mode Teams-connected sites. Owner moderated and Open modes cannot be transitioned.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Clipchamp labeling is tied to EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles

The revised sensitivity-label guidance says `EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles` controls labeling for Clipchamp projects and whether exported MP4 files inherit the project’s label. Administrators should use the tenant’s current setting value when assessing the effect.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Auto Label Insights separates progress from recorded activity

The updated guidance distinguishes periodically refreshed labeling progress from recorded labeling activity over the last 30 days. Activity counts labeling operations rather than distinct files, and the documentation points admins to the newer full review experience for daily trends.

View all updates for 17 November 2026 →

item.title: Adaptive scopes add active-only recipient and site-owner filtering in December 2026 preview — 14 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 November 2026

Adaptive scopes add active-only recipient and site-owner filtering in December 2026 preview

Two forward-looking rollouts carry the most administrator weight: adaptive scopes will shift to active-only recipient and site-owner evaluation by default, with a December 2026 preview and April 2027 general availability milestone; sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups begin in mid-January 2027. The documentation updates add targeted operational guidance on Insider Risk group-removal delays, Outlook for Mac version requirements, and failed sensitivity-label audit operations.

Purview · General

Adaptive scopes default to active lifecycle objects

Starting in the December 2026 preview, adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default, with options to include inactive or soft-deleted ones. Queries also gain ISO 8601 duration support, and general availability is scheduled for April 2027.

Purview · Labels and classification

Sensitivity labels reach Microsoft Entra cloud security groups

Beginning in mid-January 2027, sensitivity labels can be applied to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups for label-based governance and access policies. The feature must be enabled separately and requires appropriate licensing; labels cannot yet be changed or removed after application.

Insider Risk · Policies and rules

Insider Risk guidance details delayed group-removal effects

Removing a user from an included security group may not immediately stop scoring or alerting. Activities can continue contributing to alerts until processing completes, collected activities remain stored through the activation window, and existing alerts are not automatically removed. Deleted accounts in two departing-user templates continue to be monitored for the rest of that window.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Outlook for Mac 16.112 supports labels for on-premises mailboxes

The sensitivity-label guidance now specifies Outlook for Mac version 16.112 or later for on-premises mailbox support. Other Outlook clients still require Exchange Online, including when working with shared mailboxes.

Audit · General

Audit reference names failed sensitivity-label operations

The documented operation names are now FileSensitivityLabelApplyFailed, FileSensitivityLabelChangeFailed, and FileSensitivityLabelRemoveFailed. Use these names when reviewing or documenting audit events for failed sensitivity-label actions.

View all updates for 14 November 2026 →

item.title: Purview Unified Catalog guidance adds Fabric-consolidation notice and new-account restriction — 13 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 November 2026

Purview Unified Catalog guidance adds Fabric-consolidation notice and new-account restriction

The day was dominated by a retirement notice added across Unified Catalog and classic Microsoft Purview data governance guidance. Updated pages now state that these capabilities are being consolidated in Microsoft Fabric and that new accounts can no longer be created. The supplied guidance includes no migration deadline or specific migration procedure. A separate Communication Compliance update clarifies permissions for the Information Barriers SharePoint report.

Data Governance · General

Unified Catalog and classic governance pages add a retirement notice

Updated Data Governance guidance now states that Unified Catalog and classic Purview data governance capabilities are being retired and consolidated in Microsoft Fabric, and that new accounts can no longer be created. The Enterprise Glossary page supplies no deadline or specific migration step.

Data Governance · Policies and rules

Self-service policy guidance preserves existing capabilities during transition

The updated Azure SQL Database self-service policies page repeats the retirement and new-account restriction but explicitly says existing capabilities remain available during the transition.

Communication Compliance · Alerts, reports and investigation

Information Barriers report guidance names the SharePoint Embedded Administrator role

Users with the SharePoint Embedded Administrator role can run the Information Barriers SharePoint report and update segments for user-owned containers.

View all updates for 13 November 2026 →

item.title: Purview DLP guidance names Cowork while DSPM documents Copilot label-inheritance limits — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Purview DLP guidance names Cowork while DSPM documents Copilot label-inheritance limits

Cowork is the day's main thread: DLP guidance now calls the location “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork,” adds Cowork to setup examples and supported experiences, and states that administrative-unit scoping applies to Cowork for Microsoft Copilot and Chat. DSPM guidance defines when new Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and PDF content can inherit source sensitivity labels and protection. Insider Risk also clarifies alternate-email associations, while two Message Center announcements outline a mid-2027 Endpoint DLP AI capability and a late-November 2026 Edge for Business setup change.

Data Loss Prevention · AI and Copilot

DLP guidance now carries Cowork through location and scope references

The DLP location is now named “Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork,” with Cowork added to setup guidance, examples, and supported experiences. The policy reference also states that administrative-unit scoping applies to Cowork for Microsoft Copilot and Chat.

DSPM · AI and Copilot

DSPM documents sensitivity-label inheritance limits for Copilot content

The guidance says new Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and PDF content can inherit the source item's sensitivity label and protection settings. User-defined-permission labels are unsupported, and labeling does not occur when the label is unavailable to the user or the file exceeds 50 MB.

Insider Risk · General

Insider Risk explains alternate-email profile associations

Insider Risk guidance now says alternate email addresses, including Microsoft Entra ID’s Other mail values, associate activity and historical activity with user profiles. Changing an address does not correct existing alerts or historical associations.

Purview · AI and Copilot

Endpoint DLP AI skills target mid-2027 with Security Copilot required

A Message Center announcement describes AI-powered Policy Sync and Device Health skills for real-time visibility into policy deployment and synchronization issues, impacted devices, root causes, and remediation actions. The rollout is targeted for mid-2027 and requires Security Copilot enabled in the tenant.

Purview · General

Edge for Business DLP setup adds Intune multi-admin approval

Purview DLP setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will gain clearer status, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators starting in late November 2026. No policy migration is needed.

item.title: Purview retires four DSPM partner integrations December 7 as permissions auditing expands — 9 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 9 November 2026

Purview retires four DSPM partner integrations December 7 as permissions auditing expands

Microsoft Purview will retire its Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust DSPM integrations for non-Microsoft data sources on December 7, 2026. Separately, Purview is adding two audit operations for role-based access control, with worldwide rollout scheduled from late September through mid-November 2026.

Purview · General

Four DSPM partner integrations will retire

On December 7, 2026, Purview will retire the Varonis, BigID, Cyera, and OneTrust integrations for non-Microsoft data sources. They will no longer ingest or display data; other DSPM capabilities remain unaffected. Microsoft says no action is required, but administrators should review dependencies if they use these integrations.

Purview · General

RBAC permissions auditing gains two operations

Purview is adding two new audit operations for role-based access control, improving transparency and troubleshooting for access issues. The enhancement is rolling out worldwide from late September through mid-November 2026 and requires no administrator action.

item.title: DLP adds a control to exclude external emails from Copilot grounding — 6 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 November 2026

DLP adds a control to exclude external emails from Copilot grounding

A new admin-configurable Purview DLP control is described for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. It restricts processing of email from external or untrusted domains while preserving internal data use. The period also adds more precise auto-label simulation troubleshooting and a new audit activity for gateway datasource status tests.

Purview · AI and Copilot

DLP can exclude external email from Copilot grounding

The Message Center item describes a new admin-configurable DLP control for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. It excludes email from external or untrusted domains from Copilot grounding while maintaining internal data use; the item lists public preview in June 2026 and general availability in June 2027.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Auto-label guidance adds failure and partial-result handling

The Auto Label Simulation Results article adds the “Simulation failed” status, distinguishes failed jobs from requests that could not start, explains partial workload counts, and provides guidance for reviewing or restarting simulations. Administrators are told to preserve useful results before restarting and review workload details before enabling a policy.

Audit · General

Audit references gateway datasource status test activity

The Audit Log Activities reference now includes GetGatewayClusterDatasourceStatusAsAdmin for tenant administrator connection status tests, giving administrators the activity name needed to identify those tests in audit records.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Sensitivity-label guidance links simulation failure details

Apply Sensitivity Label Automatically now links to guidance for simulation failure messages and results marked “(partial)”. The change helps administrators find the relevant troubleshooting guidance when simulations fail or produce partial results.

item.title: Purview retention splits Copilot coverage; auto-labeling capped at 500,000 files daily — 5 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 5 November 2026

Purview retention splits Copilot coverage; auto-labeling capped at 500,000 files daily

Two administrator-relevant updates stand out. Beginning January 15, 2027, the “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” retention location will cover Teams content only, while updated Information Protection guidance defines 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day as an absolute aggregate ceiling across all auto-labeling policies, not a guaranteed processing rate. Related Purview pages now reflect the same ceiling.

Data Lifecycle · Policies and rules

Teams and Copilot retention coverage separates on January 15, 2027

Policies using “Teams chats and Copilot interactions” will apply only to Teams content beginning January 15, 2027. They will no longer retain or delete Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions, including previously retained interactions. Use the separate “Microsoft Copilot Experiences” location when Copilot retention is required.

Information Protection · Labels and classification

Auto-labeling throughput is an aggregate tenant ceiling, not a rate

The limit for automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files is stated as an absolute maximum of 500,000 files per tenant per day across all auto-labeling policies. Actual throughput may be lower, so administrators should assess volume across the tenant rather than treating the figure as an expected daily processing rate.
